title: Rollout velocity + warm-pool synthesis plan — NA/EU/APAC (24mo)
content:
Executive summary:

This working doc synthesizes rollout velocity planning with warm-pool sizing to deliver a pragmatic 24-month activation plan for NA / EU / APAC cloud regions. Purpose: provide a lightweight, operationally-actionable plan that connects demand signals, warm-pool sizing, expected utilization bands, and rollout gates so SRE/infra can sequence on-boarding and minimize cold-start risk during demand surges.

High-level goals:
- Ensure >= 99.9% soft availability for hosted inference routes under expected growth scenarios.
- Keep average core fleet utilization in steady-state between 60–75% (to allow headroom for burst and autoscale ramp).
- Design warm-pools to absorb 20–30% sustained surge for 48-hour windows with an additional 10% burst headroom.
- Provide clear activation triggers and rollback criteria for each regional wave.

Assumptions and inputs (short):
- Growth baseline: 1.8x ARR traffic growth year-over-year starting 2026-07.
- Model mix: 60% LLM-inference tokens (H100-optimized paths), 30% mid-size models (A100/80GB), 10% embeddings/short requests (CPU/low-gpu).
- Average request length: 280 tokens.
- Target p95 latency SLOs: 450ms for interactive gen routes, 800ms for batch/embeddings.
- Cloud GPU SKU mix used for planning: H100 (preferred for high-throughput), A100 80GB (fallback), T4/RTX for non-critical elastic workloads.
- Cost sensitivity threshold: keep incremental marginal cost per token delta <= 12% vs current baseline when activating warm-pool.

Quarterly activation timeline (24mo window):
Format: Q = quarter starting Q3 2026 (Q3-2026)

| Quarter | NA planned activation | EU planned activation | APAC planned activation | Notes |
| Q3-2026 | Warm-pool pilot (us-west2) 200 H100-equivalent | Cold standby (eu-west1) 80 A100-equiv | Observability-only (ap-southeast1) | Pilot validates warm boot time and KV-prefetching; run 6-week soak |
| Q4-2026 | Scale NA warm-pool to 600 H100-equiv; add burst lane using spare A100 nodes | Warm-pool expand to 240 A100-equiv; start canary traffic | APAC warm-pool pilot 120 A100-equiv for peak windows | 
| Q1-2027 | NA: full wave (1,200 H100-equiv) + dedicated routing policy for premium tenants | EU: scale to 640 A100-equiv; configure cross-region fallback | APAC: scale to 360 A100-equiv; enable regional KV caching | Rolling canary and auto-fallback gates active |
| Q2-2027 | NA: extend warm-pool to 1,600 H100-equiv with reserved burst 200 units | EU: full wave 1,000 A100-equiv | APAC: stretch to 720 A100-equiv | Re-evaluate utilization; may delay APAC stretch depending on spot availability |

(Summarized as text for Drive sheet consumption — table above is a planning skeleton; exact vCPU/GPU counts per node family are in linked spreadsheet stub.)

Warm-pool sizing rationale (per region):
- Warm-pool = combination of pre-warmed GPU instances + pre-populated KV cache for top-10k prefixes. Warm boot target = < 45s to reach steady throughput.
- NA: larger warm-pool allocation because of peak traffic concentration and lower network egress costs. Target steady-state warm-pool = 20% of expected steady working set Q1-2027.
- EU: moderate warm-pool sizing due to cross-region backup requirements and regulatory routing; target 18%.
- APAC: conservative initial warm-pool (10–15%) due to spot SKU variability; operational focus on warm-window scheduling aligned with APAC peak hours.

Warm-pool numeric snapshot (selected quarters):
- Q4-2026: NA=600 H100-equiv (warm), EU=240 A100-equiv, APAC=120 A100-equiv. Expected combined warm capacity = ~960 H100-equiv normalized.
- Q1-2027: NA=1,200 H100-equiv, EU=640 A100-equiv, APAC=360 A100-equiv.
- Q2-2027: NA=1,600 H100-equiv, EU=1,000 A100-equiv, APAC=720 A100-equiv.

Utilization sensitivity (three scenarios):
- Conservative (lower growth): sustained utilization 55–65%; warm-pool held but growth activation delayed one quarter.
- Base (expected): 60–75% utilization; follow timeline above.
- High-growth: 75–90% utilization; immediate stretch to next-wave capacity and accelerated procurement of additional H100s — requires exec sign-off if > 15% incremental monthly spend.

Operational activation triggers (per wave):
- Metric-based triggers: p95 latency drift > 12% for two rolling weeks OR sustained 20% traffic above 14-day MAU baseline OR queue-length spike (avg > 40ms enqueue delay) for 24 hours.
- Business triggers: enterprise onboarding with signed Dedicated contract forecasted to add > 120 H100-equivalent demand in next 30 days.
- Supply triggers: vendor availability estimate drops below 60% of requested capacity or spot price delta > 35% triggers fallback to smaller A100 mixes.

Rollback criteria (abort/rollback a warm-pool wave):
- Cost blowout: incremental marginal cost > 25% over baseline for > 7 days.
- Reliability: error rate increase > 0.8% absolute (not relative) for 48 hours after activation.
- Observability gaps: missing KV-prefill coverage > 30% for top-1k prefixes causing > 2x cold-start latencies.

Runbook highlights (short):
- Pre-activation checklist (48h): confirm image bake, KV prefill run, autoscaler ramp policies set to warm-pool thresholds, canary DNS rules ready, alert rules active.
- Activation window (timeboxed 2h): enable warm-pool, slowly shift 5% traffic every 10 minutes for first 60 minutes, monitor latency and errors.
- Post-activation soak: 72h high-fidelity monitoring (token-level tracing) and a required post-mortem template if any rollback criteria hit.

Cost control levers to apply during rollout:
- Prefer multi-tenant fractional packing where latency SLOs tolerate it (embeddings background lanes).
- Use cheap A100 nodes as burst when H100 spot premiums exceed threshold.
- Aggressive KV eviction of cold prefixes to optimize memory footprint and reduce required warm GPUs.

Open risks and mitigation:
- Vendor supply volatility (risk): maintain dual-vendor plans and staggered purchase windows; keep a 12-week optionality buffer.
- Thermal/zone capacity constraints in specific cloud zones (risk): pre-qualify two zones per region as fallbacks.
- Network egress hotspots for cross-region fallback (risk): implement route-aware throttles and regional sticky routing for enterprise SLAs.

Dependencies (quick):
- SRE: rollout automation jobs (Jenkins/GHA) — owner Derek Patel — JIRA-INFRA-4892
- Serving runtime: KV prefill tool and warm-boot hooks — owner Mariana Gomez — github.com/redwood-inference/serving/prefill#PR-211
- Procurement: contract amendments for H100 cadence — owner Finance Ops (cc Omar)

Action items (near-term):
- [ ] Validate warm-boot < 45s on H100 with real models (Alyssa + Mariana) — due 2026-07-30
- [ ] Create canary DNS policy and rollback playbook (Derek) — due 2026-08-05
- [ ] Run APAC spot-availability testbed for A100 fallback (Omar) — due 2026-08-09
- [ ] Draft exec summary for finance approval if Q1-2027 scale needed earlier (Alyssa) — due 2026-08-12

Notes to self / rough todos (working):
- Capture exact H100-equiv normalization matrix (how many A100 units = 1 H100-equiv) — handoff to capacity-cost model.
- Add a short appendix mapping to Dedicated customer onboarding SLAs and how warm-pool interacts with reserved capacity.
- Consider adding a small “edge-cache” pool in EU for low-latency customers as an experiment in Q4-2026.

Appendix (quick references):
- Performance probes to include: KV-hit ratio, prefix-cold-start rate, token-throughput per GPU, average batch size, prefill duration.
- Suggested dashboards: Cost-per-token by region, Warm-pool utilization (5/50/95), Activation event timeline with linked incidents.

This file is intentionally a working plan — expect adjustments after warm-pool pilot results. Ping #infra-capacity for syncs or if you want me to split this into the spreadsheet version (I have a draft CSV to convert).
